memory: Two-slope pattern (shallow 0.03–0.09 mm, mid 0.09–0.18 mm) and estimated knot at 0.091±0.004 mm were robust under denser sampling and skew-normal residuals. New evidence: profilometry found a 0.006±0.001 mm ridge at the contact centroid, and ultra-dense repeats show a reproducible tau_c jump aligned to that ridge. Adding a local step term removes knot significance. Skewness modeling still useful; tau_c–s1 covariance ~65%. Revision: the 0.091 mm breakpoint is likely mechanical (surface topography) rather than a smooth bulk transition. Next focus: contact-patch evolution during pushing.
